correctness.rationale: Every rotation class contains the unique edge 0101; Euler circuits are bijective with 2-choice incoming-to-outgoing edge pairings that form a single 24-edge orbit. The checker exhausts all \(2^{12}=4096\) local pairings and independently all rooted edge-use DFS tours; both sets coincide with 384 words. Each has all 24 proper four-factors exactly once. Direct rotation/reversal and all six global alphabet-permutation checks establish the counts 24, 204, 64, 34 and the four six-element reflective orbits. Separate reflection-window involution arguments prove the universal parity obstruction for all \(q\ge3\), \(k\ge3\); the finite computation is not used as proof of this infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The 384 Kautz total is established in Rosenfeld 2002 and explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. Relevant full material was inspected: Rosenfeld 2002 does not quotient by reversal; Lin et al. 2011 concerns constructions/orthogonality; Burris et al. 2016 counts different unoriented coverage objects. Actual published-finding corpus source/alias/number searches retrieved unrelated orbit tables, not equivalent Kautz reflection classes. Residual risk remains for unindexed enumeration under alternative terminology.
residual_risks: The exact first public calendar day of the 2002 Rosenfeld paper was not established, so the earliest exactly day-verified source used is the 2011-08-12 publication; this is not a claim that the underlying field began in 2011.
An unindexed finite Kautz reversal orbit table, perhaps under necklaces or chemical graph symmetry terminology, may already imply the same counts.
The all-alphabet necessary parity condition might be known as a general palindrome obstruction; the meaningful core claim is the exact first nontrivial ternary orbit census.

value.rationale: The refinement to reflective versus nonreflective Kautz cycles answers an intrinsic symmetry-classification problem left distinct from the classical enumeration: the exact 24 fixed points, 204 bracelets, four specific reflective relabeling types and 34 full isomorphism types. An elementary general obstruction explains their parity constraints. The result supplies a complete natural finite classification with reproducible independent exhaustive enumeration, rather than a routine extra total or arbitrary slice.
